candidates.lead: Manchester will receive cash from the government to help end rough sleeping by Christmas
candidates.evidence_text: £846k fund to get people off Manchester's streets by Christmas - BBC News Image source, Reuters Image caption, Funding has been given to Manchester to get rough sleepers off the streets by Christmas By Marc Waddington North West Published 2 hours ago Just under £850,000 has been given to Manchester to get people sleeping rough off the streets by Christmas. The money was handed down by the government, and comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged to end rough sleeping across the country. Manchester City Council plans to give the money to organisations that work with homeless people to help them find a "route off the streets". Figures published in March showed that the number of people sleeping rough in Manchester had increased on the previous 12 months. There were 59 people without a bed for the night, up from the previous year but lower than the March 2024 figure of 65. Tracey Rawlins, the deputy leader at Manchester City Council, welcomed the extra funding. She said: "The factors which lead to people living on the streets are complicated, so those routes cannot be 'one size fits all' and may include treatment for addiction or mental health issues and other intensive support, not only accommodation." Image source, Reuters Image caption, Burnham's "first instruction" as prime minister was to end rough sleeping In his first statement as prime minister outside 10 Downing Street in July, Burnham said: "I will soon go through that door behind me and issue my first instruction – to end rough sleeping in our country. "It's about putting the right values and the right standards at the heart of government." When he was metropolitan mayor of Greater Manchester, he pledged to end rough sleeping by 2020, and managed to reduce the figure from 268 in 2017 down to 90. But the dip also coincided with a national effort from councils to bring rough sleepers inside during the Covid-19 pandemic, and the figure began to rise again alongside increases in the cost of living. One of the organisations that will receive some of the £846,000 funding is Coffee4Craig, whose CEO Hendrix Lancaster described the prime minister's rough sleeping plans as "ballsy" during an interview shortly after Burnham's announcement in July. "I think the way he'll do it is by giving more powers to local authorities, that's worked in Greater Manchester, so why not," he said. A £442m package to provide emergency accommodation and practical support to rough sleepers around England was announced shortly after Burnham became prime minister. Ahead of the first Rough Sleeping Summit at Downing Street in October, the government indicated that a further £432m would be added to the scheme. Ten organisations in Manchester will be given a share of the city's funding, including Ancoats-based charity Mustard Tree. Deputy council leader Rawlins added: "Our voluntary, charity and faith sector partners play a hugely important role within the city in providing the range of support which people living on the streets need. "We are glad that we can use this extra funding to strengthen their work." candidates.lead: Work began on Tuesday to clear 18,000 tonnes of rubbish at an illegal dump in Bickershaw
candidates.evidence_text: Clean-up of illegal Wigan tip halted as coal mine found at site - BBC News Image source, Wigan Council Image caption, The illegal waste site is on Bolton House Road near Bickershaw, Wigan By Georgie Docker North West Published 11 November 2026 Work to clear an illegal waste dump ground to a halt on the first day after a coal mine was discovered under the site. Wigan Council said efforts to remove the 18,000-tonne pile on Bolton House Road in Bickershaw, Wigan, was stopped because of "historical mineshafts on site that could cause a risk with repeated heavy lorry loads". About 18,000 tonnes of rubbish, on Bolton House Road near Bickershaw, Wigan, had been building up since 2024. Five people were arrested earlier this year as part of the investigation into the dump, which Prime Minister Andy Burnham said had "blighted communities". . Image source, DEFRA Image caption, Wigan Council previously said removal teams would be aiming to clear up to 25 lorry loads of waste per day A council spokesperson said the contractor for the project needed to carry out further construction work "to be assured that the route is safe". The spokesperson said: "We want to reassure residents that work has started on site and this waste clearance is expected to complete in spring next year, as planned. "To avoid disruption to residents who've already suffered enough, we're accessing the site through former mining land rather than the residential road. "Due to historical mineshafts on site that could cause a risk with repeated heavy lorry loads, the contractor needs to carry out further construction work to be assured that the route is safe for this type of activity. "Works are continuing on site and we are committed to continuing to keep local residents updated as we undertake the complex work of clearing the site." The Bolton House Road site has caused concern for residents after a fire started at the site in summer 2025, forcing a nearby school to close as a precaution. candidates.evidence_text: A war memorial has been created on a roundabout by an armed forces social enterprise which provides assistance dogs for veterans The display, near Leigh Sports Village in Greater Manchester, includes 1,900 poppies - one for each of the servicemen from the Wigan area who made the ultimate sacrifice in World War One It also features 1,228 white crosses to represent members of the armed forces from the same area who were killed in World War Two and subsequent conflicts George Brooks, who launched The Reeva Programme Community Interest Company (CIC) after serving with the Army in Afghanistan, said: "We train up therapy dogs and hold events to prevent veterans from being isolated." The 35-year-old added: "When the veterans were building the memorial, the support we had from the local community was through the roof and it hits everybody who drives past, which is why we wanted to do it on a roundabout." The Reeva Programme CIC provides fully trained assistance dogs to those who have served in the armed forces or emergency services

candidates.lead: Stepping Hill's boss says the hospital in Stockport needs "at least £400m" to tackle building issues
candidates.evidence_text: Dad 'held falling lamp' during his wife's labour at Stepping Hill - BBC News Image source, Jules Wilkinson Image caption, Jules Wilkinson holds up a light that he said had fallen from the maternity ward ceiling at Stepping Hill Hospital while his wife was in labour By Kevin Fitzpatrick Greater Manchester political reporter Published 11 November 2026 A new father said he had to hold up a light that had fallen from the maternity ward ceiling while his baby was being born below. Jules Wilkinson said the lamp "started to unscrew itself" at Stepping Hill Hospital in Stockport, Greater Manchester, while his wife Lisa was in labour. The hospital's chief executive said Stepping Hill needed "at least £400m" to address building issues, while Cheadle MP Tom Morrison said he was raising the matter in Parliament. The government said Stepping Hill was receiving tens of millions of pounds for maintenance and new buildings. Image caption, Scaffolding in the main entrance to Stepping Hill Hospital Wilkinson said: "As my wife is giving birth the lamp started to unscrew itself... almost hits the midwife in the head... and literally falls out the ceiling. "It is on one of these Anglepoise arms and it just unscrewed itself." Wilkinson told BBC North West Tonight he put the lamp on his shoulders "literally hanging on by the chord" and held on to it "for the next hour or so" until his baby had been delivered. He said the maternity suites were "getting on a bit" and recalled how the birthing pools had been out of action because of a lack of heating. But he was keen to stress that "staff are doing their best". Image caption, Karen James, chief executive of the hospital trust, said it needed "at least £400m" to address identified issues Morrison and his fellow Liberal Democrat MP Lisa Smart, who represents nearby Hazel Grove, recently had a "behind the scenes" tour of the hospital. They were shown corridors with ceilings held up by scaffolding and buckets catching rainwater from leaking roofs. "What I've seen is just horrific actually," said Morrison. "This hospital has been badly let down by successive governments and it's time for this government to start acting." Smart added: "Patients are being let down. Staff are not able to give the amazing care that we know they give because the government is not funding the new buildings which would cost far less to run. "And that's what we're calling on the government to deliver." Image caption, Liberal Democrat MPs Tom Morrison and Lisa Smart were shocked by conditions at Stepping Hill Hospital Karen James, chief executive of the Stockport NHS Trust which runs the hospital, said: "Over 65% of our estate are classified in the worst categories and as time goes by the capital stock we've got - the ward areas, the estate as a whole - is getting worse every day." She said many of the buildings from the Victorian era that were not yet collapsing or leaking were also no longer fit for purpose. To meet modern standards for beds and equipment, wards in the main building would need 60% more space so to upgrade them would reduce the number of beds by more than half, she said. Rebecca Chamorto, divisional nurse director for medicine and urgent care, said conditions made life hard for staff and patients. She said: "Staff work in a confined environment with lack of storage and coming in, if it's been raining sometimes, we do get leaks so we have to check. "From a staffing perspective they come in each day with motivation and they deliver really good care despite the environment that they have got." Image caption, Scaffolding on a corridor at Stepping Hill Hospital A Department of Health and Social Care spokesperson said: "This government inherited an overstretched NHS with huge waiting lists and the hospital estate left to crumble. "Whilst decisions about local services are a matter for the local NHS, we are providing the investment and modernisation needed to get patients the care they deserve, in hospital buildings fit for purpose. "In September we confirmed £26m of funding to deliver a new pathology building at Stepping Hill, as well as a further £17m for maintenance and repair schemes, through the estates safety fund - part of £1.5bn confirmed investment so far for projects to address urgent maintenance problems across the NHS estate." They also said the trust had been allocated £75m in "operational capital" to be spent on local priorities over the next four years. Get in touch Tell us which stories we should

candidates.evidence_text: Residents living near Manchester United's stadium are calling for more to be done to tackle anti-social behaviour on matchdays - including urinating in alleyways - amid a consultation on plans to build a new 100,000-capacity ground nearby Feedback from Old Trafford residents was given to the newly set-up Old Trafford Regeneration Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) as part of the consultation Speaking at an MDC meeting, Trafford councillor Dave Acton said residents had complained to him about some fans urinating in alleyways, littering, and parking issues The MDC said it would use the responses to finalise the regeneration masterplan, due to go before the council's cabinet early next year Plans for a new stadium would see it built on the site of an indoor go-karting track in Trafford Park Acton, who represents the Gorse Hill ward, said: "We have lots of alleyways in Gorse Hill whereby the fans, unfortunately, urinate in the alleyways and this needs to be addressed."

candidates.lead: More than 40 years after the Falklands War, two veterans reunite for a new documentary
candidates.evidence_text: War veteran returns Falklands helmet to Argentina - BBC News Image source, Mick Dawson Image caption, Andy Gatrick, right, with Hector Pereyra holding his original helmet By George Carden in Rottingdean Published 11 November 2026 A former Royal Marine has reunited with an Argentine veteran to return a helmet he "borrowed" during a battle in the Falklands War. Royal Marine Andy Gatrick, who was 18 at the time, came across two injured Argentine soldiers during the Battle of Mount Harriet in 1982. The helmet belonging to one of the men, both of whom were captured by the Marines, had a name on it: Hector. Gatrick, now 63, managed to track him down and flew back on 23 October to return it. He was joined by Mick Dawson, another Royal Marine veteran from Rottingdean, East Sussex, who filmed the exchange for a new documentary called Hector's Helmet. Image source, Andy Gatrick Image caption, Royal Marine veteran Andy Gatrick, left, has returned a helmet he took during the Battle of Mount Harriet "In a very emotional day, he handed the helmet back in person to the guy he could have just as easily killed that night," said Dawson, from Rottingdean in East Sussex. Dawson, 62, told BBC Radio Sussex : "Long story short, our kit was rubbish, we had rubbish helmets that you couldn't wear. We were in berets. "They had good kit, American helmets. He borrowed one of their helmets which belonged to Hector." The two met metres from each other during the Battle of Mount Harriet, which took place on 11 and 12 June, 1982. Gatrick, from Bolton, Greater Manchester, said in footage sent to the BBC: "I put my weapon down and as I bent down to put the strap over my shoulders, I saw movement and a cloth which looked like a white handkerchief. "My eyes adjusted and there was two Argentinians, I didn't know they were badly injured. I dived to the floor, weapon up. [There was] lots of shouting and swearing, bedlam." Image source, George Carden/BBC Image caption, Mick Dawson helped film a documentary of the two veterans reuniting Hector Pereyra welcomed Gatrick and the film crew at his house in Gualeguaychu, eastern Argentina. The two "embraced like long lost brothers", said Dawson, who is originally from Lincolnshire. He added: "I interviewed Hector to get his whole story. I asked him what it was like when he was badly injured and Andy was coming out the darkness. "He said 'I knew this man had the power of life or death over me and he chose life'. That was pretty profound, he then showed me a picture of his nine grandchildren and four children that wouldn't have existed if Andy made a different decision that night. "It was just the most amazing thing to witness." There were 907 total deaths during the 74-day conflict: 649 Argentine military personnel, 255 British personnel and three civilians. Dawson said he hoped to release the documentary next year. Follow BBC Sussex on Facebook , external , X , external , and Instagram , external and listen to BBC Radio Sussex on Sounds . candidates.what_happened: War veteran returns Falklands helmet to Argentina
candidates.source_evidence: A former Royal Marine has reunited with an Argentine veteran to return a helmet he "borrowed" during a battle in the Falklands War Royal Marine Andy Gatrick, who was 18 at the time, came across two injured Argentine soldiers during the Battle of Mount Harriet in 1982 The helmet belonging to one of the men, both of whom were captured by the Marines, had a name on it: Hector. Gatrick, now 63, managed to track him down and flew back on 23 October to return it He was joined by Mick Dawson, another Royal Marine veteran from Rottingdean, East Sussex, who filmed the exchange for a new documentary called Hector's Helmet "In a very emotional day, he handed the helmet back in person to the guy he could have just as easily killed that night," said Dawson, from Rottingdean in East Sussex Dawson, 62, told BBC Radio Sussex : "Long story short, our kit was rubbish, we had rubbish helmets that you couldn't wear. We were in berets

candidates.evidence_text: A war memorial has been created on a roundabout by an armed forces social enterprise which provides assistance dogs for veterans The display, near Leigh Sports Village in Greater Manchester, includes 1,900 poppies - one for each of the servicemen from the Wigan area who made the ultimate sacrifice in World War One It also features 1,228 white crosses to represent members of the armed forces from the same area who were killed in World War Two and subsequent conflicts George Brooks, who launched The Reeva Programme Community Interest Company (CIC) after serving with the Army in Afghanistan, said: "We train up therapy dogs and hold events to prevent veterans from being isolated." The 35-year-old added: "When the veterans were building the memorial, the support we had from the local community was through the roof and it hits everybody who drives past, which is why we wanted to do it on a roundabout." The Reeva Programme CIC provides fully trained assistance dogs to those who have served in the armed forces or emergency services

candidates.evidence_text: A Cumbrian band who were the first British outfit to tour war-torn Ukraine is behind a star-studded gig in aid of women and children impacted by the conflict Hardwicke Circus have toured twice across music venues, hospitals and prosthetic centres in Ukraine since the war's outbreak They are behind Songs Of Freedom, a gig featuring Bob Geldof, Madness and Peter Hook, to be held at Manchester's Co-Op Live on 3 February and streamed worldwide Sir Paul McCartney, Barbra Streisand and Sean Penn will appear via video link at the event. It will be promoted by Harvey Goldsmith, who promoted Live Aid in 1985, organised by Geldof and Midge Ure to raise money for famine relief efforts in Ethiopia Hardwicke Circus' singer and guitarist Jonny Foster said it was "fantastic" to see so many big names support the idea, which the band came up with in the back of their tour van "I'm from Carlisle, I'm not in them circles whatsoever, but we were motivated by our tours of Ukraine."

The 26-year-old has now been jailed. candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre 14 beautiful photos as Manchester commemorates Remembrance Day We will remember them View 15 Images 1 of 15 (Image: Kenny Brown | Manchester Evening News) Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 14:25, 11 Nov 2026 The war memorial in St Peter's Square in Manchester city centre was crowded today (November 11) as around 200 people turned out to mark Remembrance Day Students, office staff and construction workers massed around the marble memorial alongside police officers, veterans and members of the armed forces community, where wreaths of poppies were laid and a speaker read out an excerpt from Laurence Binyon's poem For the Fallen The poem reads: "They shall grow not old, as we that are left grow old / Age shall not weary them, nor the years condemn. / At the going down of the sun and in the morning / We will remember them." A maroon was then fired as a bugler played the Last Post to mark the beginning of the two minutes' silence at 11am, which was carefully observed, with the only sound in the busy square the trundle of passing trams Members of Manchester city council including Lord Mayor Shaukat Ali, chief executive Tom Stannard and council leader Garry Bridges then laid poppy wreathes on the memorial and a soprano performed I Vow To Thee, My Country before the national anthem was sung

But will crumbling Stepping Hill Hospital finally be saved? 'We've had a succession of ministers who have said the righ Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 17:22, 11 Nov 2026 Updated 06:48, 12 Nov 2026 The situation at crumbling Stepping Hill Hospital – where bosses are pleading for cash to stop patients’ safety being put at risk – is ‘extremely worrying’, Earlier this week, NHS bosses in the Stockport yet again urgently appealed for funds to stop the hospital estate falling further into disrepair. The site has seen significant upgrades in recent years – including new multi-million emergency and outpatient departments – but many of Numerous areas are decrepit after 121 years treating patients. More than half the estate is deemed to be in ‘poor’ or ‘bad’ condition One medic said wards are ‘falling apart’, claiming some buildings ‘need to be condemned’. Patients sometimes have to be transferred elsewhere or have surgeries cancelled, they add, with the ‘snowball effect’ making waiting times worse Pictures inside show disintegrating walls; leaking roofs; and precarious floors. Damp plagues areas of the estate; water trickles from windows when it rains; and some staircases are closed

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester The very different lives of ordinary Mancunians in neighbourhoods eight miles apart A new report has lifted the lid on the impact of deprivation in Manchester. View 3 Images Harpurhey and Didsbury centres (Image: Manchester Evening News) Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 17:10, 11 Nov 2026 Updated 06:48, 12 Nov 2026 Around eight miles separates Harpurhey and Didsbury in Manchester. It’s a journey that can take 30 minutes by car, driving past the Etihad Campus and gleamin Despite how close they are, the two areas are on opposite sides of a scale of poverty and deprivation. Harpurhey was ranked the most deprived part of Manchester in the 2025 indices of deprivation, alongside Gorton and Abbey Hey, and Miles Platting and Newton Heath Didsbury, Deansgate , and Chorlton sit on the other side of the rankings, making up the least deprived parts of the city A new report published by Manchester council reveals the ‘stark’ inequalities between the city's communities and the impact that divide is having on the lives of ordinary Mancunians The report said boys born to mums living in the city’s most deprived areas are likely to live eight years less than those born in Manchester’s least deprived neighbourhoods. For girls, the life expectancy gap is slightly less at seven years

candidates.evidence_text: Bury ‘Serious safety failings’ found in Bury council social housing inspection, watchdog warns The council could not show it was meeting the ‘legally required timescales’ to investigate, identify and repair hazards such as damp and mould, while 2,800 Outcomes in safety and accountability were judged to be particularly poor, with the Regulator of Social Housing saying it cannot be sure the town hall is meeting its legal duties. The town hall owns around 7,600 homes with some 300 of these managed by an external agency It was the council’s first inspection under the regulatory framework and it was awarded a C3 rating – the second lowest outcome. The council took its housing services back into direct management in 2024 as it began to wind down social housing provider Six Town Housing (STH) It is in the process of consulting on the future of the remaining around 100 homes managed by STH, with a recent report recommending that these too be brought under the council control. The council believes that will offer ‘greater long-term stability’ for tenants, with alternati Among the concerns raised by inspectors were overdue fire safety remedial actions, with 2,800 outstanding at the time of the inspection. While most were assessed as being low to medium risk, the Regulator of Social Housing said there was a ‘lack of clarity’ about the time taken t The council also could not show it was meeting the ‘legally required timescales’ to investigate, identify and repair hazards such as damp and mould

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre 14 beautiful photos as Manchester commemorates Remembrance Day We will remember them View 15 Images 1 of 15 (Image: Kenny Brown | Manchester Evening News) Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 14:25, 11 Nov 2026 The war memorial in St Peter's Square in Manchester city centre was crowded today (November 11) as around 200 people turned out to mark Remembrance Day Students, office staff and construction workers massed around the marble memorial alongside police officers, veterans and members of the armed forces community, where wreaths of poppies were laid and a speaker read out an excerpt from Laurence Binyon's poem For the Fallen The poem reads: "They shall grow not old, as we that are left grow old / Age shall not weary them, nor the years condemn. / At the going down of the sun and in the morning / We will remember them." A maroon was then fired as a bugler played the Last Post to mark the beginning of the two minutes' silence at 11am, which was carefully observed, with the only sound in the busy square the trundle of passing trams Members of Manchester city council including Lord Mayor Shaukat Ali, chief executive Tom Stannard and council leader Garry Bridges then laid poppy wreathes on the memorial and a soprano performed I Vow To Thee, My Country before the national anthem was sung

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Mum involved in drug smuggling plot that saw man, 20, die in Dubai hotel room, trial told Five people - including Jensen Westhead's mum and stepfather - deny his manslaughter Add to preferred sources News Rachel Smith Court reporter and Greta S A drugs mule who flew from Manchester Airport died in a Dubai hotel room after a package of cocaine he had swallowed burst open in his stomach, a court has been told Jensen Westhead was found at the Avalon Hotel on December 5, 2024, the day after he arrived in the United Arab Emirates, an ongoing trial at Preston Crown Court has heard. Five people, including Westhead's mother, deny manslaughter and drugs offences Among those in the dock are Jensen's mother, Rebecca Hatch, and her partner Glenn Hatch. The prosecution allege Mr and Mrs Hatch assisted the conspiracy by helping Jensen renew his passport and taking him to the airport - knowing the purpose of his trip to Dubai, Lancs Live repor The other defendants are Alexander Tofton, who the prosecution say was the UK arm of the international smuggling operation, and who is alleged to have recruited Jensen into the conspiracy Joseph Watson is alleged to be the Dubai arm of the conspiracy and met with the courier when he arrived in the Emirates, a trial opening heard yesterday (November 10)

He was last seen 'running away' from a petrol station on Bolton Road in Kearsley, Bolton, at around 7.30am the morning before, Sunday, August 7, 2016 Greater Manchester Police said he hasn't been seen since and a subsequent investigation established he was murdered and his body disposed of 'by criminals known to him'. candidates.evidence_text: Newton Heath Teenager who saved neighbour, 14, from burning bedroom as home engulfed in flames hailed a hero 'We owe Joe everything' Add to preferred sources Comments News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Writer and Chris Slater Senior Reporter 17:44 A teenager who saved his 14-year-old neighbour from her burning bedroom as flames engulfed her home has been hailed a hero by her family. But modest Joe Frere, 17, insists: "I just did what I think anyone should do." A fire broke out at the home Tracey Jones shares with three of her children in Newton Heath last Tuesday evening (November 3). Her daughter Rai was in her room after getting home from school She locked her door to get changed, lit a candle and fell asleep. Rai woke up to find the room filled with smoke after a fire broke out. Her mum had gone out to drop her grandson off somewhere Alone in the house, Rai screamed for help from her window. She said she thought she was going to die. Her desperate shouts for help were heard by neighbour Tilly Smith, who rang 999. Tilly ran to alert Joe and his family, whose house backs onto Edgeware Road where Rai and her fam Joe said he 'didn't think' when he heard his family friend was in trouble and leapt from the sofa. The selfless teenager ran to Rai's house and saw the flames as smoke billowed from the roof

'We've had a succession of ministers who have said the righ Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 17:22, 11 Nov 2026 Updated 06:48, 12 Nov 2026 The situation at crumbling Stepping Hill Hospital – where bosses are pleading for cash to stop patients’ safety being put at risk – is ‘extremely worrying’, Earlier this week, NHS bosses in the Stockport yet again urgently appealed for funds to stop the hospital estate falling further into disrepair. The site has seen significant upgrades in recent years – including new multi-million emergency and outpatient departments – but many of Numerous areas are decrepit after 121 years treating patients. More than half the estate is deemed to be in ‘poor’ or ‘bad’ condition One medic said wards are ‘falling apart’, claiming some buildings ‘need to be condemned’. Patients sometimes have to be transferred elsewhere or have surgeries cancelled, they add, with the ‘snowball effect’ making waiting times worse Pictures inside show disintegrating walls; leaking roofs; and precarious floors. Damp plagues areas of the estate; water trickles from windows when it rains; and some staircases are closed

candidates.evidence_text: Bury ‘Serious safety failings’ found in Bury council social housing inspection, watchdog warns The council could not show it was meeting the ‘legally required timescales’ to investigate, identify and repair hazards such as damp and mould, while 2,800 Outcomes in safety and accountability were judged to be particularly poor, with the Regulator of Social Housing saying it cannot be sure the town hall is meeting its legal duties. The town hall owns around 7,600 homes with some 300 of these managed by an external agency It was the council’s first inspection under the regulatory framework and it was awarded a C3 rating – the second lowest outcome. The council took its housing services back into direct management in 2024 as it began to wind down social housing provider Six Town Housing (STH) It is in the process of consulting on the future of the remaining around 100 homes managed by STH, with a recent report recommending that these too be brought under the council control. The council believes that will offer ‘greater long-term stability’ for tenants, with alternati Among the concerns raised by inspectors were overdue fire safety remedial actions, with 2,800 outstanding at the time of the inspection. While most were assessed as being low to medium risk, the Regulator of Social Housing said there was a ‘lack of clarity’ about the time taken t The council also could not show it was meeting the ‘legally required timescales’ to investigate, identify and repair hazards such as damp and mould

View 3 Images Harpurhey and Didsbury centres (Image: Manchester Evening News) Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 17:10, 11 Nov 2026 Updated 06:48, 12 Nov 2026 Around eight miles separates Harpurhey and Didsbury in Manchester. It’s a journey that can take 30 minutes by car, driving past the Etihad Campus and gleamin Despite how close they are, the two areas are on opposite sides of a scale of poverty and deprivation. Harpurhey was ranked the most deprived part of Manchester in the 2025 indices of deprivation, alongside Gorton and Abbey Hey, and Miles Platting and Newton Heath Didsbury, Deansgate , and Chorlton sit on the other side of the rankings, making up the least deprived parts of the city A new report published by Manchester council reveals the ‘stark’ inequalities between the city's communities and the impact that divide is having on the lives of ordinary Mancunians The report said boys born to mums living in the city’s most deprived areas are likely to live eight years less than those born in Manchester’s least deprived neighbourhoods. For girls, the life expectancy gap is slightly less at seven years

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Council Manchester council facing £5.5m black hole The council's finances are under major pressure. Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 19:18, 11 Nov 2026 View 2 Images The council's budget was discu Manchester council has a £5.5m black hole to plug in its finances - with the city facing major pressure from spending on adult social care, housing, and education, health and care plans The figure was published in the council’s latest update on Wednesday (November 11) over its revenue budget - money used to fund essential services Adult social care funding is under huge strain and the council has an overspend of £9.4m, which has been partially offset by underspending in other departments The council said in its report: “The overspend relates to sustained increases in demand and rising complexity of care packages, particularly in supported accommodation “Workforce pressures, including temporary agency usage to cover vacancies, sickness and leave, further contribute.”

As cops arrived at the home in Fallowfield, a shocked householder told officers: "He's still in my house." When officers went into the property, they saw prolific burglar Fazal Alnensi, who sheepishly stood up from a chair he was sitting on and smiled as he coolly said 'hello' When he was pointed out as a thief, he was arrested on suspicion of burglary and led away. The 26-year-old has now been jailed. The householder returned to his home in Fallowfield at around 2.25am on June 12 this year, to find Alnensi inside Michael MartinThe burglar claimed he was only there because he wanted a glass of water but he refused to leave and officers who were called subsequently found a set of car keys belonging to the homeowner in his pockets Alnensi had been 'rummaging' through drawers in the property, according to Greater Manchester Police

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre 14 beautiful photos as Manchester commemorates Remembrance Day We will remember them View 15 Images 1 of 15 (Image: Kenny Brown | Manchester Evening News) Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 14:25, 11 Nov 2026 The war memorial in St Peter's Square in Manchester city centre was crowded today (November 11) as around 200 people turned out to mark Remembrance Day Students, office staff and construction workers massed around the marble memorial alongside police officers, veterans and members of the armed forces community, where wreaths of poppies were laid and a speaker read out an excerpt from Laurence Binyon's poem For the Fallen The poem reads: "They shall grow not old, as we that are left grow old / Age shall not weary them, nor the years condemn. / At the going down of the sun and in the morning / We will remember them." A maroon was then fired as a bugler played the Last Post to mark the beginning of the two minutes' silence at 11am, which was carefully observed, with the only sound in the busy square the trundle of passing trams Members of Manchester city council including Lord Mayor Shaukat Ali, chief executive Tom Stannard and council leader Garry Bridges then laid poppy wreathes on the memorial and a soprano performed I Vow To Thee, My Country before the national anthem was sung

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Mum involved in drug smuggling plot that saw man, 20, die in Dubai hotel room, trial told Five people - including Jensen Westhead's mum and stepfather - deny his manslaughter Add to preferred sources News Rachel Smith Court reporter and Greta S A drugs mule who flew from Manchester Airport died in a Dubai hotel room after a package of cocaine he had swallowed burst open in his stomach, a court has been told Jensen Westhead was found at the Avalon Hotel on December 5, 2024, the day after he arrived in the United Arab Emirates, an ongoing trial at Preston Crown Court has heard. Five people, including Westhead's mother, deny manslaughter and drugs offences Among those in the dock are Jensen's mother, Rebecca Hatch, and her partner Glenn Hatch. The prosecution allege Mr and Mrs Hatch assisted the conspiracy by helping Jensen renew his passport and taking him to the airport - knowing the purpose of his trip to Dubai, Lancs Live repor The other defendants are Alexander Tofton, who the prosecution say was the UK arm of the international smuggling operation, and who is alleged to have recruited Jensen into the conspiracy Joseph Watson is alleged to be the Dubai arm of the conspiracy and met with the courier when he arrived in the Emirates, a trial opening heard yesterday (November 10)

Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

Credit: via planning documents Councillors sided with officers on all four major applications on the planning committee’s agenda on Thursday, which was good news for Story Homes, Russell, and Bellway – and not so great for Barratt and David Wilson Homes Woodford Garden Village underwent a series of changes from its original proposals, with councillors ultimately voting in favour of the building of up to 423 homes, up to 72 fully affordable extra care apartments, and a 72-bed care home on a 75-acre site off Chester Road The plans also include 1,100 sq ft of retail space, a 6,500 sq ft health centre, and a 6,500 sq ft day nursery with outdoor space. There would also be a mobility point with cycle parking, parcel lockers, and a bus stop Russell’s plans include a 16-acre nature park that could hold nature trails, allotments, an orchard, and children’s play area. This, combined with open space allocated around the site, leads to ta total open space provision of 24.7 acres Looking at the housing plans, up to 248 homes would be affordable. This includes the 72 extra care apartments. Of those 248 homes, 22% are envisioned as social rent, 13% for affordable rent, and 65% for affordable ownership

candidates.evidence_text: Anyone who has lived in Greater Manchester for more than a winter knows that planning for the weather is part of everyday life. That’s as true at Christmas as at any other time, and it shapes the way many local families think about presents: something for the wet days, something This year’s guide takes that approach. It’s about choosing presents that last beyond Boxing Day, and pairing them with the kind of days out the region does well The best Christmas presents are the ones that are still being played with in February, when the decorations are down and the evenings are long. That tends to mean open-ended toys, ones that don’t need batteries or instructions and that children can use in a dozen different ways Imaginative play is the classic example. A good range of kids dolls offers soft-bodied dolls for toddlers, posable figures for older children, and everything in between, and the right one can be a companion for years. Younger children do best with something sturdy and washable, w If you’re buying for a child who’s likely to be tired, over-excited and surrounded by relatives on Christmas Day, ease of use counts for a lot. A doll set that arrives with furniture, outfits and accessories can be played with the moment it’s unwrapped, with no hunting for missin Check the contents before you buy. Accessories that work with other toys in the house are the most useful, and flexible pieces beat single-purpose props that are forgotten by January

candidates.evidence_text: Michael Martin, from Salford, was reported missing on 8 August 2016 after the then 25-year-old was last seen at a petrol station on Bolton Road , in Kearsley, Bolton, the day before Ten years on, detectives investigating his murder have offered the reward to try find his body His father, Gregg Martin, said the "not-knowing is gut wrenching every day" and added: "We know he's dead but it's just not knowing where he was, where he is and what happened to him. It'd give the family some closure – a form of sort of peace." He added: "My message to the people is to do the right thing – tell someone or indirectly let the police know what happened to Michael so we can get some peace of mind and closure." Greater Manchester Police has treated the investigation as a "non-body murder" since 2016 The renewed appeal for information leading to Martin's body comes after, in 2018, police offered £50,000 for information on Martin's disappearance

candidates.title: Everything you need to know about Oldham's Christmas Lights Switch-On 2026
candidates.summary: A fun-packed programme of free festive fun is coming to Oldham on Saturday

candidates.practical_angle: Есть новый городской контекст для Greater Manchester.
candidates.lead: A fun-packed programme of free festive fun is coming to Oldham on Saturday
candidates.evidence_text: Everything you need to know about Oldham’s Christmas Lights Switch-On 2026 | Oldham Council Father Christmas waving to the crowds at last year's switch on Published: Wednesday, 11th November 2026 A fun-packed programme of free festive fun is coming to Oldham on Saturday. The countdown is almost over as Oldham prepares to kick off the festive season with its annual Christmas Lights Switch-On. Visitors are invited to the town centre this Saturday (14 November) for a day packed with free family entertainment and festive activities. The town is hosting an exciting calendar of entertainment as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture 2026 to showcase the very best of Oldham's culture, creativity and community spirit. Here's everything you need to know ahead of this year's celebrations. Family fun starts from 1pm The day begins at Spindles from 1pm, with activities hosted by the Spindles Kids Club and special appearances from everyone's favourite pig, Peppa Pig, outside Next on the ground floor of Spindles. Families will have the chance to wave hello to Peppa and take photos at 1pm, 2pm and 3pm. There will be craft activities near Vision Express and face painting near the YMCA charity shop from 12pm to 4pm. Switch-On Show begins at 5.30pm The festive celebrations move to Parliament Square from 5.30pm for the main Switch-On Show. Residents can enjoy an evening of festive entertainment featuring Father Christmas, Peppa Pig's Dance Party, Oldham Rock Choir and Fierce Dance. The Mayor of Oldham, Councillor Pam Byrne, will join the celebrations and a local school child competition winner will take centre stage to switch on the Christmas lights. Fireworks finale The evening will end with a spectacular fireworks display, with a festive lights and laser show. Free parking It will be even easier for people to join in the festivities, with free parking in all council town centre car parks from 3.30pm. So wrap up warm, bring your friends and family and step into Christmas. Peppa at the cinema To coincide with the switch on, the Festive Fun with Peppa Cinema Experience is coming to the Odeon at Parliament Square on Saturday 14 and Sunday 15 November, at 10am, 11.30am and 1pm both days. Join Peppa Pig and her family at the cinema for a festive big-screen experience as they celebrate Evie’s first Christmas. To book click here. The festive celebrations will continue throughout December with a series of themed weekend events. The festive fun doesn't stop there On Saturday 5 December, visitors can enjoy Brass Monkeys in the town centre, bringing together local and national brass bands. Running from 11am until 4pm. the event celebrates Oldham's rich brass band heritage with performances ranging from traditional Christmas carols to funky strolling street bands. The following weekend, on Saturday 12 December, the town centre will be transformed for Winter Wonderland Saturday. Running from 12pm until 4pm, the event will feature a host of festive characters, family entertainment and music, including the Winter Fairy, Betty Twinkle, Winter Wonderland Birds, The Snow Patrol, Lairy Fairy, Dancing Christmas tree and the Bouncing Snowmen, alongside activities from the Spindles Kids Club. The festive programme will conclude on Saturday 19 December with Santa Saturday, a magical family day filled with seasonal entertainment. Between 12pm and 4pm, visitors can encounter Wish Fairies, Festive Funky Hooping, Circus Elves, Rockin' Robins, Bad Santas and Glitter Belles as they bring festive cheer to the town centre alongside Christmas music from local Brass Bands. A special celebration as Greater Manchester's Town of Culture Oldham Council's Director of Communities Neil Consterdine said: "Oldham's Christmas Lights Switch-On is one of the highlights of our calendar, and this year feels particularly special as we celebrate our year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture. "This is a fantastic opportunity to bring people together, support our town centre and showcase the creativity, talent and community spirit that make Oldham so unique. "We're looking forward to a great atmosphere and are encouraging residents and visitors to come along and enjoy everything our town centre has to offer." To view our full programme of upcoming events visit whatson.oldham.gov.uk News archive Oldham Council news RSS feed

The awards recognise the borough’s success in horticulture, Following the outstanding gold achievement and scooping the overall Town Centres and City Centres title at the recent Royal Horticultural Society Britain in Bloom awards, Rochdale town centre’s horticulturists remained on their winning streak taking gold and best in category for Rochdale in Bloom treasurer Phil Massey also received an outstanding contribution award for his significant work supporting Rochdale’s success in both national and local efforts Baillie Street Quarter won the new Best Art in the Community award for outstanding artwork from the recent Common Walls International Mural Festival, organised by talented local artist Hayley Garner (Ayo). Rochdale BID also secured gold and won the Best Business Improvement Distr Hampton by Hilton hotel entered for the first time this year, taking gold and category winner, alongside a gold for nearby Norton Grange hotel in the Large Accommodation category

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Streets in Bolton are set to be cleaner after the council invested in new equipment to tackle litter, leaves and fly-tipping New road sweepers have been purchased, bigger bins installed at key spots and handy equipment stores provided for volunteer litter pickers A fleet of road sweepers in various sizes are used by the council to remove leaves and litter, and there have been several recent additions One large sweeper has been added, making three in total, and these are vital for keeping roads and drains clear of leaves and twigs in autumn, which reduces the risk of flooding as well as keeping streets looking tidy Six smaller mechanical sweepers are used on pavements, with teams focusing on different areas of Bolton on a rotating schedule A new electrically powered pavement sweeper has also been brought in that can get into smaller spaces like cycle lanes, helping to keep them clean and safe to use

candidates.evidence_text: Pupils across Bolton returning from the summer holidays last month were greeted by safer and warmer classrooms after the council invested in the borough’s schools Working with local employers Seddon, the council oversaw repairs and improvements at more than half a dozen schools, benefitting over 3,000 pupils from primary to secondary age The wide-ranging work was carried out over the summer break to minimise disruption The project saw some schools receiving new boilers and water heaters, new roof installed at one primary school, while another had more energy efficient windows installed Some fire alarm systems and emergency lighting have also been upgraded It is the second school decarbonisation project Seddon has delivered with Bolton Council, helping to improve the efficiency and long-term sustainability of school buildings across the borough

candidates.evidence_text: Alfie and family with Wigan Council and Bethell representatives at the Wigan Road crossing An eleven-year-old boy concerned about the safety of a busy main road has seen his request for a pedestrian crossing become a reality A frequent visitor to Ashfield Park in Standish, Alfie Haywood grew increasingly concerned about crossing Wigan Road to access the park, particularly when he was on his way home from school or crossing with his family and younger sister Encouraged by his nan Ruth, Alfie wrote a letter to Wigan Council and Lisa Nandy MP to raise his concerns and request a safer crossing, resulting in a toucan crossing being installed, along with improved road infrastructure for motorists, pedestrians, and cyclists Alfie, a pupil at St Peter’s High School in Orrell, said: “The reason I wanted this crossing is because lots of children and families visit Ashfield Park, but because this is such a busy road, somebody might get run over and hurt, and a crossing will allow people to cross the roa “I feel very proud and confident that the council listened to my idea, and I would like other children to know that they can help their community to become a better place

The band, who had two top five albums in the UK charts in the mid-90s and are most known for their iconic anthems ‘Things Can Only Get Better’ and ‘U R The Best Thing’, will headline the stage The event will also feature a packed schedule of free music and entertainment, and everyone will be able to enjoy Wigan’s Christmas lights switch-on Sunday 22nd November is also the last chance to visit Light Night Wigan, a fabulous trail of beautiful light installations across Mesnes Park and town centre venues. Tickets are needed to access the Mesnes Park part of Light Night Wigan

Honouring Our Communities reflects this belief by shining a light on the people and places that have shaped our lives, identities and creative journeys. Through a collection of artworks by Black artists At HOME Arches the three artists on show are C.Talah with 'It was never just me' (2026), Damaris Edey with 'Rooted in the hands of many' (2026) and Mux Imagery with 'AYOBAMI' (2025) C. Talah (Courtney Hammond) is a Manchester-based artist whose work is inspired by identity, heritage and the people around her. Her Jamaican and British background often comes through in her work, alongside themes of family, memory and community. 'It was never just me' (2026) lo Damaris Edey is a self-taught visual artist born in Manchester, with Caribbean heritage. Her emotional portraits celebrate the divine, authentic beauty and vibrancy of Black women, while exploring the chaotic nature of life through expressive mixed media. Layers of texture create Mux Imagery is the visual practice of photographer Abiola Badmus, focusing on identity, culture, and storytelling. candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . Everyone’s welcome, regardless The pop-up is open Friday from 10am to 4pm, Saturday from 10am to 6pm and Sunday from 11am to 4pm. Whether you’re hunting down a rare pair or just fancy a Saturday morning run followed by a pastry, there’s plenty of reason to swing by

candidates.evidence_text: Having recently dropped his latest album, We Are Together Again, gothic/alt country musician and actor Bonnie Prince Billy is indeed together with you all, right here at Albert Hall in Manchester, on the 16th of November However dimly we perceive it, we are living through a change of worlds. candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. Born in London into a Gambian griot lineage of seven centuries, she began learning the kora at age three with her brother Tunde Jegede and father Sanjally Jobarteh; her cousin was the late Toumani Diabaté. She studied at the Royal College of Music, the Purcell School of Music and SOAS University of London. In 2015 she founded The Gambia Academy, which puts African history and culture at the centre of its curriculum, and she has keynoted forums hosted by the UN and the World Trade Organization. In 2023 Berklee College of Music awarded her an honorary Doctorate in Music alongside Usher and Roberta Flack

candidates.evidence_text: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument. Please email learning@bandonthewall.org if you have any questions about this course

candidates.evidence_text: The Olllam is a band that fuses Irish traditional music with the modern jazz/post-rock energy of Detroit. Led by uilleann piper John McSherry, the band features Joe Dart (Vulfpeck), Michael Shimmin, Ross Ainslie, Seán O’Meara, and Joe Hettinga. Following their acclaimed album elllegy (RTÉ Radio 1 Best Group), The Olllam has collaborated with GRAMMY-nominated producer Zedd, shared the stage in Belfast with actor Anthony Boyle (Netflix’s House of Guinness), and recently completed a landmark U.S. tour in November 2025. From ancient airs to future soundscapes, The Olllam is not just carrying the tradition forward—they’re reinventing it

candidates.lead: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867.
candidates.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

It is Open Restaurant Group’s ninth restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Didsbury in Sep At the focus of the restaurant is a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, which places guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors feature four-metre elm trees, curved booth seating and a brass wine display, so the atmosphere and experienc Award-winning Andrew Sheridan brings his internationally inspired approach to Counter, building on a career that has seen multiple restaurants under his direction feature in the prestigious Michelin Guide. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot and From the grill, guests can enjoy the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside the slow-cooked Thai Lamb Shoulder, served with red thai sauce, chilli and coriander

Cadno Lounge, Neath . Loungers, the West Country‑based café‑bar group, will open Fosforo Lounge, King Street in Stretford on Saturday 28th November 2026, creating around 30 new jobs for local people.. . Fosforo Lounge will be open all day, every day, serving breakfast, brunch, lunch, dinner and drinks, with dedicated kids’, gluten‑free and vegan menus. . The site on King Street has been transformed by the Loungers design team into a warm, eclectic ‘home from home’ – their signature style. Fosforo translates to matchstick and is a nod to Manchester-based painter LS Lowry’s ‘matchstick men’ style.. . Fosforo Lounge’s all‑day menu will cater for every taste, from hearty comfort food to healthier choices and indulgent treats. Families are a major focus, with games, books, colouring materials, high chairs and baby‑changing facilities available for Little Loungers.. . With community at its heart, Fosforo Lounge will offer a welcoming space for regular meet‑ups, business catch‑ups, book clubs, knitting groups, parent‑and‑baby sessions, creative workshops and more. Local groups looking for a friendly, flexible venue will be encouraged to get in touch.. . Vix Connolly, General Manager, Fosforo Lounge said: “We’re so looking forward to welcoming everyone to Fosforo Lounge on the 28th November. Becoming a genuine part of the community is incredibly important to us, and we can’t wait to meet our neighbours and get involved locally.. . “If you’re looking for a friendly, flexible space for events or group meet‑ups, pop in once we’re open – we’d love to chat and see how we can help.”. . . . . . . evidence_packet.evidence_text: Hilton House keeps proving itself as one of the borough's best creative hubs and this August it's hosting a community music night. PINK's Summer Open Mic is being put on by local guitar shop Rigby Music, with covers and originals welcome from anyone who wants to give it a go Alongside the music, fellow Hilton House residents Spearpoint Vintage are setting up a pop-up of pieces from their collection, available to buy on the night, with the chance to book in for a future appointment at their showroom too It's a relaxed one — no pressure, just a room of people who like music and a rail of good vintage to pick through between sets Where: PINK, Hilton House, Lord Street, Stockport SK1 3NA When: Wednesday 5 August 2026, 6:45pm–10pm Want to perform? Email admin@rigbymusic.co.uk Know of an open mic or pop-up we should be covering? Let us know — we're always up for a Wednesday night out in the borough

candidates.lead: Posted by Manchester Digital Introducing The Inside Track: A new way to get more from your Manchester Digital membership
candidates.evidence_text: Stay connected. Know what's next. We're launching The Inside Track , a new monthly online session designed to help Manchester Digital members stay informed, discover new opportunities and make the most of their membership Whether you've recently joined Manchester Digital or have been part of our community for years, The Inside Track is your chance to catch up with our team, find out what's happening across the network and explore ways to get more involved Taking place on the last Wednesday of each month, these free, members-only sessions will bring you up to speed on the latest developments, events and opportunities across Manchester Digital, all in just 30 minutes Each session will feature a topical focus, alongside practical updates on upcoming events, programmes, speaking opportunities and ways to raise your business's profile There'll also be time to ask questions, share your priorities and find out how we can help you get more value from your membership Our first edition at midday on 25th November will focus on some of the biggest opportunities coming up across the Manchester Digital community

candidates.evidence_text: Legal AI leader Clio expands global footprint in Salford - Invest Manchester Skip to main content Skip to footer Opens in a new tab Digital, cyber & AI , Financial, professional, business services Legal AI leader Clio expands global footprint in Salford Published on November 11, 2026 News Clio , the global leader in legal AI, expands its UK presence with a move to Eden , having signed a deal with ECF to take the first fitted and furnished suite in Manchester’s highly sustainable, 12-storey workplace in New Bailey . Moving from Alderley Edge, Clio’s new 5,134 sq. ft office is a turnkey space designed for high-growth businesses, with 50 fixed workstations, dedicated pods and booths for focused work, board and meeting rooms, a kitchen complete with a dining area, and flexible touchdown spaces built to support collaboration. Already home to law firm TLT, accountancy and business advisory firm BDO, and the PE-backed professional services group Leonard Curtis, Eden offers move-in-ready office space designed to make taking on a new workspace simpler and more straightforward. Delivered by ECF, our partnership with Homes England’s National Housing Bank, L&G and Muse , the turnkey model streamlined Clio’s move into its new space, reducing the time and complexity typically associated with a traditional office fit-out. Moving into a city centre location brings Clio closer to its growing UK customer base following its recent acquisition of Manchester-based ShareDo, now Clio Operate , the legal work management platform for large firms and enterprise legal teams. Eden’s central location and modern amenities also support Clio’s continued growth by strengthening its ability to attract and retain talent. Following the successful letting of its first fitted and furnished workspace, ECF is now underway with two additional suites within Eden, delivered to a similar specification. The first of the two new suites will be available from December 2026, with the second scheduled to be available from early 2027. This will include a 4,886 sq. ft office on the same floor as Clio, and a 10,000 sq ft. space on the second floor, with ECF responding to continued demand for turnkey solutions of this nature across the sector. Organisations that move to Eden send a clear message that they’re committed to fostering a healthy, connected and collaborative workforce centred around wellness and wellbeing, along with demonstrating their ambition to create a sustainable future. Eden itself is home to a range of amenities, including on-site café, Spice & Grind, a yoga/contemplation studio, and a roof terrace, each designed to offer occupants space to take a break from day-to-day work schedules. Elsewhere there are enhanced fresh air rates which boost cognitive function; there’s an emphasis on natural light and planting to provide a connection to nature; and the whole building embraces the WELL Building Standard Principles to create a workplace that supports productivity and collaboration. In-keeping with Eden’s green credentials – which include being net zero carbon in operation – the new fitted and furnished suite has been designed with sustainability at its heart too, enabling the space to become the first fit-out in the UK to achieve both SKA V2 Gold certification and a Net Zero Aligned approach. This is in part thanks to a range of specific fixtures and furnishings which have been prioritised to incorporate high levels of circularity. This includes the use of cork for its renewable and recyclable properties, utilisation of 100% of the CAT A lighting, and the specification of recycled denim for elements of the kitchen chairs. Eden’s sustainability credentials and its focus on employee wellbeing were significant factors in Clio’s decision. Laura Percy, development director, said : “Welcoming Clio to Eden’s first fitted and furnished suite represents another significant staging post in this remarkable building’s journey, and we’re delighted to support Clio’s growth as it takes this next step. “Being part of Eden offers a working experience unlike any other, with a strong focus on connectivity, collaboration, wellbeing and sustainability. It is the ideal place for businesses looking to build a brighter future for both the company and its team. “Since its completion in 2024 Eden has become a Manchester landmark, with a green wall façade adorned with 350,000 plants. candidates.evidence_text: Cloud Imperium Games Expands VERSA Studios Partnership with Squadron 42 Showcase - Invest Manchester Skip to main content Skip to footer Opens in a new tab Creative & media , Digital, cyber & AI Cloud Imperium Games Expands VERSA Studios Partnership with Squadron 42 Showcase Published on November 9, 2026 News Cloud Imperium Games (CIG), developer of Squadron 42 and Star Citizen, brought an exclusive Squadron 42 showcase to VERSA Studios Manchester, building on its established presence in the city. The event was one of Manchester’s major media events of the year, bringing gamers and streamers from around the world to experience the highly anticipated game ahead of its release next year. Star Wars actor Mark Hamill, one of the game’s stars, also attended in October. VERSA supported CIG in delivering the event and co-produced the behind-the-scenes filming, including interviews with the game’s creators. More details about the filming will be shared soon. More than 40 people worked on the project, with VERSA coordinating the crew, lighting, production design, sound, studio space and other production requirements. VERSA also brought in specialist virtual production partner Mars Volume, which built the largest virtual production screen ever constructed in Manchester and created immersive content inspired by the game. A life-sized Hornet spacecraft provided by CIG was also part of the environment. Sandi Roberts, Co-Founder of Cloud Imperium Games , said: “We had a wonderful experience working with VERSA and its teams to bring our event to life.” The project showcases VERSA Studios Manchester’s capabilities across virtual production, motion capture and wider production services. Charlie Ingall, Executive Director of VERSA Studios, said: “This project shows how VERSA works as a production partner, bringing together people, technology, facilities and specialist partners across gaming, physical production and virtual production. Working with CIG, our team helped deliver an ambitious event and co-produce the behind-the-scenes filming on a feature-film scale. It’s a strong example of the scale of what can be delivered at VERSA.” CIG has an established presence at St John’s, the landmark Manchester district developed by Allied London, where it is based in the UK. It also has a permanent motion-capture studio at VERSA Studios Manchester, one of the largest of its kind in the UK. Allied London is the parent company of VERSA Media Group, which operates VERSA Studios in Manchester, Leeds and London. candidates.evidence_text: A special evening celebrating one of Manchester’s most influential musicians, Vini Reilly and his post-punk project The Durutti Column, comes to Albert Hall this month Fresh from sold-out Southbank Centre performances, a unique ensemble will reinterpret key works from The Durutti Column’s remarkable six-decade career in Reilly’s home city on Thu 19 Nov Presenting the one-night-only For Vini show is producer Keir Stewart, who has worked with Reilly and drummer Bruce Mitchell since 1998’s Time Was Gigantic… When We Were Kids album For the performance, Stewart (guitar, bass, samples, keys) is joined by The Durutti Column collaborators Sam Morris (French horn), Caoilfhionn Rose (vocals and piano) and Liz Rossi (violin and piano) Audiences can expect to hear material that spans releases on Factory Records through to tracks from Renascent , creating a rare and immersive live experience that honours one of Manchester’s most singular musical voices, one recently cited as a key influence on Harry Styles’ late Coinciding with the homecoming show at Albert Hall, The Durutti Column have joined with Four Tet for an official remix of Your Shadow at Morning. You’ll also be invited to the opening day celebrations with music across three stages at Stoller Hall Earlybird wristbands sold out in record time. Second-release wristbands are now on sale, with the next price increase due in late November, so secure yours now to get the best value. You can also buy individual concert tickets for headline shows

The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . candidates.lead: Bolton Car Boot Sale at Bolton Car Boot Sale
candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. Last confirmed: 10 September 2026 Event date: 2026-11-15 Venue: Bolton Car Boot Sale Price: £1 Status: https://schema.org/EventScheduled

Презентація максі-синглу "Живий" Кожного разу, коли перед менеджментом гурту Бумбокс стоїть завдання написати пресреліз, ми починаємо згадувати цікаві факти. Скільки концертів зіграли, скільки грошей зібрали, які пісні видали. Це база. Непогано ще пам’ятати, чи був гурт у країні, до якої ми збираємося, чи це пер О, як би хотілося написати: "Концерт гурту Бумбокс" — і як у Львові за добу продано 8000 квитків. Так-так, ми не про Львів розповідаємо, хоча теж про Європу Наші віддані слухачі, якщо ви перебуваєте за кордоном, сподіваємось, вам буде цікаво дізнатися, що після традиційної перерви на декілька місяців, Бумбокс поїде в турне від Ізраїлю до Німеччини, від Англії до Польщі, від Ірландії до Словаччини та Чехії І повеземо ми в це турне свіженький, як херсонський кавун, максі-сингл “Живий”, підсилений піснями з різних альбомів, під частину яких виросли ви, а під частину зростають ваші діти Тож ознайомтеся, будь ласка, уважно з розкладом туру, купуйте квитки заздалегідь, готуйте гроші на донати та мерч — зустрінемося в листопаді
